entries.summary: Private Studio borrowed-reference operation. Authoring close is a no-op for a live borrowed reference: it preserves the target and other aliases. A null or stale reference reports an access error. Reference input and Error input/output; no reference output or array lifting. Object-operation graph execution has no runtime provider in this delivery.

Private Studio configuration of one exact method signature. Parameters retain their identities, types, input/output directions, requirements and declared defaults; a void method has no result terminal. The incoming object reference determines the effective class. The authoring provider supports only advertised real operations; unavailable focus and panel actions remain explicit. Reference and Error pairs stay fixed. No object-operation graph runtime provider is available in this delivery.

Private Studio configuration of ordered property rows. Each stable row chooses one real member and Read or Write; its data terminal follows the complete member type. An incoming object reference takes precedence over the implicit symbolic target. Real authoring provider access checks target permissions, latch Value and contained-widget restrictions. Reference and Error pairs stay fixed; Value (Signaling) and graph execution are unavailable in this delivery.

Private Studio symbolic reference constant for This Frog, This Application, Front Panel or a widget identified by its owner document and stable identity. The single reference output is distinct from the widget data value and preserves a complete strict schema when known. Class upcasts are allowed; a generic reference does not implicitly become strict. Saved files contain no native handles. Resolution uses the live authoring provider; graph runtime execution is unavailable in this delivery.

entries.title_en: DB Tools Load Recordset From File.vi
entries.summary: Loads a recordset from a file and returns a recordset reference that identifies this recordset. You can retrieve data from this recordset like any other recordset, but some properties might not be available on this recordset.

entries.summary: Moves the cursor to point to the next record in the recordset identified by the reference. Wire data to the reference input to determine the polymorphic instance to use or manually select the instance.

entries.title_en: DB Tools Move To Previous Record.vi
entries.summary: Moves the cursor to point to the previous record in the recordset. You cannot use this VI with a forward-only cursor. Wire data to the reference input to determine the polymorphic instance to use or manually select the instance.

entries.title_en: DB Tools Move To Record N.vi
entries.summary: Moves the cursor to point to record n in the recordset. To move the cursor to the last record, set n to -1. You cannot use this VI with a forward-only cursor. Wire data to the reference input to determine the polymorphic instance to use or manually select the instance.

Typed FIFO resource operations. Queue<T> is the shared access reference, not a message or a Front Panel object reference. Each message retains its complete type.

Removes and returns the head element in FIFO order. An empty queue waits cooperatively: -1 means no deadline, 0 an immediate attempt. Ordinary timeout is distinguished from invalidation and from a successfully received message. Queue<T> is an execution resource reference; element is the ordinary T value. Public FROG target compilation remains unavailable.

Adds one element at the tail. A full bounded FIFO waits cooperatively for space: timeout -1 waits indefinitely, 0 attempts immediately. Expiration inserts nothing. It never silently evicts an element; invalidation interrupts the wait with an error. Queue<T> is an execution resource reference; element is the ordinary T value. Public FROG target compilation remains unavailable.

Atomically removes the present messages and returns them in FIFO order, preserving each complete message boundary even when T itself is an Array. The queue stays valid and usable; an empty FIFO returns an empty outer array. Queue<T> is an execution resource reference; element is the ordinary T value. Public FROG target compilation remains unavailable.

Atomically evicts the oldest element only if a bounded FIFO is full, then appends the new element without waiting. The overflow element is meaningful only when overflow? is true. Ordinary Enqueue does not use this lossy behavior. Queue<T> is an execution resource reference; element is the ordinary T value. Public FROG target compilation remains unavailable.

Creates an anonymous FIFO when name is empty, or obtains an additional access to a same-application named FIFO with exactly the complete element type. The type specimen is not an inserted message. Capacity defaults to -1; an existing named capacity is preserved. Queue<T> is an execution resource reference; element is the ordinary T value. Public FROG target compilation remains unavailable.

Returns the head element without removal or reservation. An empty FIFO waits cooperatively using timeout -1 by default. A successful preview does not prevent another consumer removing that message. Queue<T> is an execution resource reference; element is the ordinary T value. Public FROG target compilation remains unavailable.

Releases this obtained access, preserving independently obtained accesses unless force destroy is true. Forced destruction invalidates all accesses and wakes waits with errors. Cleanup also executes with an incoming error. Returns the FIFO snapshot before release and never returns a queue reference. Queue<T> is an execution resource reference; element is the ordinary T value. Public FROG target compilation remains unavailable.

Reads a coherent instant snapshot: name, capacity, count and waiting operations. Preview and dequeue both count as pending removals. Elements are returned only when requested, without removal; otherwise that output is an empty array. Queue<T> is an execution resource reference; element is the ordinary T value. Public FROG target compilation remains unavailable.
